_comment: Copy this to .claude/settings.json in your project root. Adjust SOURCE_DIRS in scripts/check-lld-exists.sh to match your layout.
_hook_path_note: Hook commands use "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR" so they resolve regardless of the hook's working directory. Never use bare repo-relative paths like 'bash .claude/hooks/X.sh' — they throw 'No such file or directory' when the hook cwd is not the project root.
_permissions_note: Keep this list SHORT. Three rules, the first two measured against a live session:
1. Output redirection rides along on a match. `cmd > file` and `cmd >> file` are permitted by a
rule for `cmd`, and an EXACT entry with no wildcard does not help. So every entry grants
'write this command's stdout to any path'. Never allowlist a command whose output is
attacker-controlled — `gh issue view` is the sharp one: issue bodies are untrusted, and
`gh issue view N -q .body > .git/hooks/pre-commit` is a working chain.
2. Command chaining (`&&`) and each segment of a pipe ARE checked, so those are not the risk.
3. Never allowlist an interpreter, shell, or package manager. `python`, `python3`, `node`, `bun`,
`npx`, `pip`, `bash` and friends are arbitrary code execution. A previous version of this file
allowed python, python3, pip, semgrep, `git *` (which includes `push --force`) and `gh *`
(which includes `gh api --method POST`). It was never installed by anything, which is the only
Most read-only commands (cat, ls, grep, head, tail, find, and every read-only git and gh
subcommand) are auto-allowed by Claude Code already and need no entry here.

_hook_modes._comment: Set LLD_HOOK_MODE in env above. warn = log but allow writes. block = hard block writes with no LLD.
_hook_modes.warn: Use during initial rollout — teams see the warning but can still write
_hook_modes.block: Use once manifest + LLDs are complete for all active domains
